key_insight: InftyThink+ uses reinforcement learning to adaptively manage iterative chain-of-thought reasoning, learning when to summarize, what to keep, and how to resume so models can reason indefinitely with far lower cost and less degradation.
problem_solved: Addresses the quadratic cost, context-length limits, and "lost-in-the-middle" degradation of scaled chain-of-thought inference by replacing fixed or supervised summarization heuristics with an RL-driven, memory-aware control policy.
method: Train an RL controller that decides when to compress intermediate thoughts, what content to store in a compact memory, and how to resume reasoning from summaries.
Use a learnable summarization/compression module to produce compact, relevant memory entries and a resumption strategy that integrates preserved context with ongoing chain-of-thought.
Optimize a reward balancing final-answer accuracy and computational/memory cost to enable long-horizon, efficient reasoning.
impact: Enables LLMs to perform long, iterative reasoning with much lower compute and reduced degradation, making reliable multi-step inference practical for resource-constrained or long-context applications.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: input → iterative reasoning loop → RL controller (decide summarize/resume) → compressed memory → resumed reasoning
Timeline illustration: long chain-of-thought with periodic summaries vs. naive expanding context (showing cost growth and lost-in-the-middle)
Performance vs. cost chart: accuracy or reasoning quality vs. token/context cost comparing InftyThink+, fixed heuristics, and no-summarize baselines
Icon set: RL policy (agent), memory/compression (archive), accuracy (target), efficiency (speedometer)
paper_title: InftyThink+: Effective and Efficient Infinite-Horizon Reasoning via Reinforcement Learning
paper_authors: Yuchen Yan, Liang Jiang, Jin Jiang, Shuaicheng Li, Zujie Wen
